Complex multi-part animations (e.g. an explainer video with an interactive clock widget, a split-screen physics simulation, and independent timelines) are difficult to manage within a single monolithic scene graph.
Retiam provides the [`SubScene`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/SubScene.ts) entity, which enables **Scene-in-Scene nesting**:

items: **Complete Encapsulation**: A sub-animation is authored as a standalone [`Scene`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/Scene.ts) with its own camera, animations, coordinate axes, and lifecycle.

**Hierarchical Scene Graph Mounting**: The `SubScene` wraps the child scene as a standard [`Entity`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/Entity.ts), allowing it to be positioned, rotated, scaled, anchored (`nextTo`, `alignTo`), and animated via the master scene.
**GPU Resource Bridging**: Automatically shares the parent scene's WebGPU device, compute dispatch queues, state managers, and render pipelines, eliminating duplicate VRAM initialization.

blocks.text: When a `SubScene` is added to a parent scene graph, its `update(t, dt)` cycle establishes the GPU bridge upon its first frame:

items: **Compute Dispatch Queue (`compute_queue`)**: GPU compute tasks requested by the child scene (such as Chaikin curve smoothing or instanced layout computation) are multiplexed into the parent's command encoder pass.
**Global State Allocator (`stateManager`)**: State uniform memory slabs (256-byte blocks) are allocated from the parent's unified GPU buffer pool.
**Invalidation Chaining**: When a child entity mutates its transform or color, `invalidate()` bubbles up to the parent `SceneComposer`, triggering a redraw without requiring polling.
